snippets.text: vLLM shipped version 0.30.0, built from 762 commits by 315 contributors, 104 of them first-timers.
snippets.why: vLLM is the engine most open-weight models are served on, so its release notes set what those models can do in production.

snippets.text: Qwen-Image-2.1 now tops the open-source models on both the Image Edit and Text-to-Image arenas, Alibaba's Qwen team says.
snippets.why: The 7B model went out with open weights on Sunday, which puts a model anyone can download at the top of both lists.

snippets.text: Cursor says Claude Opus 5.5 is the new top model on CursorBench at 57.8% and costs 40% less per task than Opus 5.
snippets.why: CursorBench is Cursor's own test, so this is one vendor's measurement, but Cursor is where many developers will use the model.

snippets.text: Perplexity says Opus 5.5 scored 0.610 on its WANDR benchmark at $4.13 a task, slightly ahead of Fable 5.1 at 67.6% lower cost.
snippets.why: If the figure holds, most of Fable 5.1's performance at about a third of the price changes which model agent products default to.

snippets.text: GitHub made OpenAI's GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna generally available in Copilot, with Luna as the lowest-cost option.
snippets.why: Both launched the same day in OpenAI's API at half the price of GPT-5.6, and Copilot is where most developers will meet them.

snippets.text: StepFun's StepAudio 3 ASR took first place on Artificial Analysis's non-streaming speech-to-text index, with a 1.7% word error rate.
snippets.why: That is down from 4.7% for its predecessor, and lands in the same week StepFun put out its Step 5 Preview language model.

snippets.text: Ollama says some requests to deepseek-v4.1-flash were billed at the wrong rate for a few hours, and has apologised to affected users.
snippets.why: If you ran that model on Ollama's hosted service this week, the post explains how the affected usage is being handled.

snippets.text: Perplexity says training its Computer agent to learn from its own errors cut tool-call failures by 21.2% in a live A/B test.
snippets.why: The method, hint-guided self-distillation, trains the agent on its own failed attempts rather than on fresh human labels.

snippets.text: Moonshot renamed Kimi WebBridge the Kimi Browser Extension, which can record a task's steps once and save them as a reusable skill.
snippets.why: Recording a workflow once and replaying it is what turns a browser chat assistant into something that does repetitive work for you.

snippets.text: Artificial Analysis launched a benchmark for how reliably text-to-speech models pronounce hard text. Google's Gemini 3.1 Flash TTS leads at 88.1%.
snippets.why: Names, numbers and technical terms are the words voice agents get wrong, and this is a test built to measure exactly that.

snippets.text: The Hacker News says Next.js patched a critical ImageResponse flaw, CVE-2026-94545, that can run code on the server; versions 16.2.0 to 16.3.5 on Node.js are affected and 16.3.6 fixes it.
The Hacker News says a phishing kit sold at $320 a month, NovaCookies, relays Microsoft 365 logins in real time and captures the session after multi-factor authentication succeeds.
Techmeme says German publisher C.H. Beck has taken a majority stake in Noxtua, a legal-drafting AI firm that raised a Series C of more than $100 million, citing Tech.eu.
Bloomberg says Chinese chip foundry CanSemi Technology is seeking about $919 million in an initial public offering on the Shenzhen exchange's ChiNext board.
Counterpoint Research puts global AI glasses shipments up 263% year on year in the first half of 2026, driven by Meta and EssilorLuxottica's display-less line, Techmeme says.
Israeli prime minister Netanyahu says he is setting a goal for Israel to become the third AI power after the United States and China within five years.
alphaXiv flags RRSI, a paper that constrains how self-improving agent harnesses evolve; it says the method lifts out-of-distribution scores while using 30% fewer policy tokens.
AWS says Claude Opus 5.5 is now available on Amazon Bedrock and on the Claude Platform on AWS, the day after Anthropic released the model.
AWS says GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna are generally available on Amazon Bedrock, giving customers two more OpenAI options to match cost to workload.
Simon Willison shipped llm 0.36, adding gpt-6-sol and gpt-6-luna, and a flag letting plugins declare that a model accepts only single-turn prompts.
Simon Willison released llm-anthropic 0.29, which adds Claude Opus 5.5 to the LLM command-line tool.
The Hacker News says F5's BIG-IP APM has a zero-day, CVE-2026-94127, exploited for unauthenticated remote code execution. F5 has issued hotfixes and CISA added it to KEV.
The Hacker News says Chinese threat actor UTA0565 chained three Chrome-Windows zero-days to escape the browser sandbox and deploy CLEANGULP malware from fake sites.
Techmeme says NADI, a new Dutch government agency modelled on DARPA, has opened a 40 million euro challenge on AI-assisted chip design with Germany's SPRIND.
Reuters says the OECD credits AI-led investment with holding the global economy up slightly better than expected this year, while the energy shock weighs on 2027.
Bloomberg says Wrtn Technologies, one of South Korea's fastest-growing AI startups, has picked Mirae Asset Securities as lead underwriter for a planned IPO.
Testing Catalog says OpenAI is preparing Free, Prototype and Accelerate plans for its platform, with Accelerate starting at $50 for higher rate limits on production apps.
Testing Catalog says SpaceXAI is building a Remote Control feature for Grok on web and mobile, and that iOS strings point to a Grok Desktop app.
UBS started coverage of AI data centre stocks at buy, putting Core Scientific at $24 and saying AMD-backed capacity gives it a path to a 3-gigawatt platform.
seveibar asked Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Sol to design a USB-PD stepper controller fitting on the back of a NEMA17 motor, using tscircuit, as a one-shot with no schematic cleanup.
techartist_ says Opus 5.5 built a house in Three.js and TSL that grows through four stages, from first lines to massing, detail and finished home.
Tyler Nishida says his favourite Opus 5.5 build is a personal origami tool he drives from Claude, importing designs from Figma, the web or code and tuning the interactions.
chongdashu says Opus 5.5 helped build a browser game where the player is a pressure washer, shipped in Rust, Wasm and WebGPU with assets from Blender and Tripo.
paoloanzn says he built wilwid, a Chrome extension that strips content you dislike from every page in real time, using Opus 5.5 with TypeSafe's Jev model.
marmaduke091 says Opus 5.5 one-shot an Xbox controller in 334 lines of SVG with the logo drawn correctly, and calls it a token monster at maximum effort.
argofowl asked Opus 5.5 at extra-high effort for an endless procedurally generated Three.js world to roam, with surprises everywhere however long the player stays.
Jerry Liu says Opus 5.5 made the teaser video for DocJev, an open-source tool for classifying and splitting complex document packets.
Articus_chad asked Opus 5.5 to make something it was interested in making, and says it produced a visual explanation of emergence.
MaxBlade says Opus 5.5 built a multiplayer lawn-mowing simulator that he ran live on his own server for viewers to join.
Yanqing Cheng ran Opus 5.5 against GPT-6 Sol on one prompt for a visualisation of the Mongol conquests from an already-researched dataset, and says it was not close.
tonbistudio says Opus 5.5 built a bonsai tokonoma in Three.js from a prompt by majidmanzarpour, and rates the result above Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra.
Google Cloud says Claude Opus 5.5 is available in Vertex AI Model Garden, for long-running coding and knowledge work at a lower cost per task.
Design Arena says Claude Opus 5.5 is now on its leaderboard, where the public votes on full-stack and game-development outputs from competing models.
Min Choi collected ten Opus 5.5 builds in a thread that passed 500 likes, opening with a Dark Souls clone, and says people cannot stop building.
chetaslua says Opus 5.5 one-shot a detailed comparison website and held its cost at 272,000 tokens, where he says GPT-6 Sol becomes expensive.
